summary: Performed a final verification of the Run 3 interpretability smoke-test implementation for the KUL LOSO Conformer pipeline. The review failed because methodological claims were not supported by executable verification, documentation diverged from implementation, and a regression was introduced between dynamic channel ablation output and downstream plotting.
lessons: Keep downstream analysis and visualization synchronized with dynamically generated experiment outputs to avoid implementation regressions.
Ensure documentation accurately reflects the implemented algorithm; implementation-documentation mismatches invalidate scientific claims.
Do not rely on comments to establish dataset or checkpoint provenance; methodology claims require executable verification.
Do not present exploratory perturbation analyses as validated physiological interpretations unless they are justified by the validated evaluation protocol.
Validate all reported baseline metrics used as acceptance criteria before proceeding with downstream interpretability analyses.
Treat unsupported methodological assertions as research risks even when the implementation executes successfully.
Verify checkpoint compatibility with the evaluation dataset before drawing interpretability conclusions.
Resolve implementation inconsistencies before accepting interpretability results, even if earlier runtime issues have been fixed.
task: Run 3 Smoke Test Interpretability suite implementation - Final Check
